messages:
PagerDuty Bot: [P0] High error rate - TLS handshake failures (inference-api). Triggered at 2026-06-12T03:14:00Z. Pager: @Infra Oncall, @Carla N, @Sam T
Carla N: I'm here, seeing a spike of 524/525 from clients in us-west-2. LB logs show 'TLS handshake failure' repeatedly.
Sam T: Oncall ack, pulling envoy logs now. Are we seeing a single cert name or many?
Deepak S: I can confirm source is rproxy-prod edge. Error: "tls: handshake failure" and also "tls: no certificate" in some streams.
Marta P: CS heads up — some enterprise customers on dedicated pools are reporting dropped streaming responses. Severity P0 for affected customers.
Infra Oncall: Taking lead. Handoff: I'm infra-oncall, will collect timeline and coordinate mitigation. Any recent infra change?
Carla N: There was a cert rotation last night via ops/rotate-certs job (job id 7842). Rotation reported success across regions.
Ryan L: Attaching snippet from envoy on node rproxy-34: ```[2026-06-12T03:12:43Z] envoy auth: TLS error: "tls: no certificate" peer CN=client1 source_ip=10.0.5.23
[2026-06-12T03:12:43Z] envoy connection: TLS handshake failed: remote error: unknown certificate
[2026-06-12T03:12:44Z] listener '0.0.0.0:443' accepted connection from 10.0.5.23
```
Sam T: Running quick checks: `openssl s_client -connect rproxy-prod-usw2:443 -servername api.redwood.com` returns "no peer certificate" from one node, while another node returns full chain.
Carla N: Which nodes differ? Was the rotation batched? Rotation job parallelized across rproxy ASG with rolling restart.
Deepak S: Rotation used the new cert chain with Let'sEnc CN chain (longer chain). Hypothesis: some rproxy hosts missed the new chain or have incomplete chain file.
Marta P: Customer impact matrix: streaming sessions failed to establish TLS; non-streaming requests (short API calls) mostly ok. That points to middlebox/MTU possibly.
Infra Oncall: Noted. Two hypotheses to track: H1 - partial cert rotation left some nodes with missing intermediates. H2 - network MTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello or cert to be dropped mid-handshake.
Carla N: Evidence for H1: rotation logs show node rproxy-34 returned exit code 0 but agent logs show `write of /etc/ssl/certs/fullchain.pem failed: no space left on device` on 03:08Z for one replica. Maybe that replica kept old cert or partial file.
Ryan L: Evidence for H2: tcpdump from rproxy-34 shows many retransmits and MSS 1400 on peering link. Partner VPC peering had an MTU change scheduled earlier for other teams?
Sam T: Running `ip link` on worker -> MTU 9001 on our side; peer reports 1500. If the ClientHello or cert packet exceeds 1500 and DF set, fragmentation could fail. I'm seeing a pattern where connections with larger TLS cert chains fail.
Deepak S: Good catch. Some clients negotiate large ClientHello due to SNI + TLS extensions + large certs; if path MTU misconfigured, the handshake can stall/fail.
Marta P: Which mitigation is fastest with least blast radius?
Infra Oncall: Short term: enable fallback to the previous smaller cert chain (rollback rotation) on a small canary set to validate. Also route traffic away from nodes with signs of missing certs. Longer term: fix MTU mismatch with peering partner.
Carla N: I'll prepare a canary rollback for rproxy-34 ASG - rollback to old fullchain (job id 7838) and set healthcheck to drain then replace.
Sam T: I'll add iptables rule to temporarily lower TCP MSS to 1400 on rproxy nodes (`--clamp-mss-to-pmtu`), that often fixes middlebox fragmentation issues without full MTU change.
Ryan L: Running `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and applying `tc qdisc` clamp on canary nodes now.
CS Bot: Notifying impacted customers: we sent an initial incident message to affected enterprise contacts and pointed to status.redwood.com.
Carla N: Canary rollback started at 03:28Z for rproxy-34 ASG. Rolling back certs on 2 instances.
Ryan L: After applying MSS clamp and cert rollback to one canary, metrics show TLS handshake success rate improved from 18% to 96% on that canary in 5 minutes.
Deepak S: Correlating logs: nodes with updated firewall rules + clamp show no "no certificate" errors. Nodes without clamp still show handshake failures.
Infra Oncall: Good — mitigation path validated. We'll perform region-wide clamp + staged rollback for affected ASGs.
Marta P: CS update queued: "Mitigation in progress, partial rollback and network clamp applied, some customers restored. ETA 30-60m."
Sam T: While we fix, let's document timeline: 03:05Z cert rotation job 7842 ran (rolled on rproxy), 03:08Z agent on rproxy-34 reported disk write error during rotation, 03:12Z handshake errors spike, 03:20Z MTU mismatch detected on peering, 03:28Z clamp applied & canary rollback, 03:34Z success on canary.
Carla N: I'm creating a log bundle with `/var/log/ops/rotate-certs-7842.log`, `journalctl -u rproxy`, and tcpdumps from peers, will upload to S3 and link.
Ryan L: Paste of critical tcpdump snippet showing retransmits and ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' from peer: ```IP 10.0.5.23.49152 > 10.0.6.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
ICMP 10.0.6.1 unreachable - fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu 1500)```
Deepak S: That ICMP clearly points to MTU issue. Coupled with partial cert files we saw, the handshake can fail either because server couldn't send full chain back or client hello didn't reach. Two contributing factors.
Infra Oncall: RCA draft: simultaneous partial cert rotation (failed write on some hosts) plus an unnoticed MTU mismatch on VPC peering triggered TLS handshake failures for connections requiring larger TLS messages. Root cause = race of cert rotation + network MTU misconfig.
Marta P: Impact summary for postmortem: 47 customers impacted transiently, highest impact on streaming sessions using dedicated pools. Mitigations: revert to smaller cert chain on affected nodes + apply TCP MSS clamp cluster-wide + coordinate MTU fix with peering partner.
Carla N: Action items I'm logging: 1) Improve cert rotation validation to verify fullchain presence and test TLS handshake before marking job success. 2) Add healthcheck to detect TLS handshake failures quickly. 3) Schedule peering MTU audit with networking partner.
Sam T: I'll author the in-incident timeline and hypothesis table in the postmortem doc. Marking H1/H2 as confirmed/contributing.
CS Bot: Sent second customer update: majority restored, small percentage still affected. Support triage active.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident status changed to MOVING TO MITIGATION at 2026-06-12T04:00:00Z.
Infra Oncall: Closing loop — rolling cluster-wide application of MSS clamp starting now, and cert rollback finishing. Will monitor for 30m then transition to recovery and RCA write-up.
Ryan L: Final check: `curl -v https://rproxy-prod-usw2/api/health` returns HTTP/200 and TLS negotiated with correct chain on all checked nodes.
Carla N: Thanks team. I'll follow up with full postmortem with timeline, logs, and remediation plan.
Sam T: I'll follow with deployment changes to rotation job (preflight handshake test).
Marta P: I'll update customers when RCA is published.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident resolved at 2026-06-12T05:10:00Z — mitigation validated. Incident ticket: INC-20260612-1972.
